newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says Commission cannot suspend customs duties.
newsitem.headline: Court says Commission cannot suspend customs duties.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday the Council of Ministers has the authority to suspend customs duties on fishery products, but the European Commission does not.
The court also said residual customs duties on imports of tuna preserved in olive oil from Spain to Italy in 1991 and 1992 cannot be suspended under the Act of Accession of Spain and Portugal.

Whether tax authorities are prohibited from collecting duties post-clearance of the goods at issue depends on three conditions: the competent authorities must have made a mistake, the importer could not have reasonably detected the mistake, and the importer must have acted in good faith by providing a full declaration.
The national court must review the facts of each case to determine whether post-clearance recovery of customs duties is possible.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Italian)

Eight references to the Court from the Tribunale di Genova for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings between

on the interpretation of article 1(1) of Commission regulation (EEC) No 3416/91 of 25 November 1991 on certain residual duties applicable in 1991 in the framework of the successive reduction in accordance with the Act of Accession of Spain and Portugal (OJ 1991 L 324, p. 11) and of article 5 of Council regulation (EEC) No 1679/79 of 24 July 1979 on the post-clearance recovery of import duties which have not been required of the person liable for payment on goods entered for a customs procedure involving the obligation to pay such duties (OJ 1979 L 197, p. 1)

1. The suspension of the residual customs duties applicable to imports from Spain into the Community of Ten in accordance with article 75(1) of the Act of Accession, provided for in article 1(1) of Commission Regulation No 3416/91 on certain residual duties applicable in 1991 in the framework of the successive reduction in accordance with the Act of Accession of Spain and Portugal for the agricultural products listed in the Annex to Council Regulation No 3835/90 in respect of the system of generalised tariff preferences applied to certain products originating in Boliva, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, does not apply to imports of preserved tuna in olive oil from Spain.

2. It is for the national court to establish whether the conditions laid down in article 5(2) of Council Regulation No 1679/79 on the post-clearance recovery of import duties which have not been required of the person liable for payment on goods entered for a customs procedure involving the obligation to pay such duties are fulfilled. In determining whether or not the error committed by the authorities could reasonably have been detected by the person liable account should be taken, in particular, of the nature of the error, the professional experience of the trader concerned and the degree of care exercised by him. The relevant factors to be taken into account include the complexity of the legislation, the terms in which the objective of the provisions at issue is expressed, recurrence of the error in question in other measures of the member state concerned and any divergence of views between the member state as to the proper interpretation of the relevant provisions.
